title: Cutover Watchlist — Night Owl Slate (Apr 2027)
content:
Context and intent:
- Short one: overnight capacity-driven release that touches routing policies, autoscaler config, and the backend KV cache rollout. We need a compact watchlist for night-shift operators and a skeleton release notes block that can be pasted into the public channel after cutover.
- Why night: lower traffic window for global customers, but elevated risk for APAC markets. Keep the APAC fallback lane primed.

Goals:
- Flip autoscaler config 00:30 UTC with zero-traffic ramp for the first 20 minutes.
- Validate 95th latency unchanged within 20% of baseline for first 60 minutes.
- No data-plane errors above 0.05% for the first 2 hours.

Scope (what is changing)
- Routing policy update: prefer 2nd generation g-quant models for batch path (feature flag toggle).
- Autoscaler threshold shift: target_cpu -> 60% (was 45%).
- KV cache serialization change rolled to 50% of nodes initially.
- No schema changes to API surface. Client SDKs unaffected.

Quick roll timeline (UTC) — condensed watchlist for night crew
- 00:00  Ops check-in: gather on call, confirm owner roster (lines below).
- 00:05  Preflight smoke: token-level cost check, critical traces baseline snapshot, deploy snapshot of canary.
- 00:15  Enable 10% KV cache serialization change via canary route. Monitor 00:15-00:45.
- 00:30  Flip autoscaler to new thresholds. Keep canary on for 30m after flip.
- 00:45  Increase KV cache rollout to 50% if canary healthy.
- 01:00  Enable routing policy toggle 10% traffic to new batch path.
- 01:30  If telemetry green, escalate to 100% batch path for non-critical tiers.
- 02:00  Finalize rollout for reserved capacity pools; start post-release validations.

Preflight checklist (must be green before 00:00)
- [ ] Pager duty roster confirmed and contactable (uzones + phone).
- [ ] Night shift bridge link created and pinned in #release-ops.
- [ ] Baseline metrics captured: 95th latency, error rate, token cost, and unit throughput.
- [ ] Smoke test suite (smoke/sanity.sh) passes locally on canary image.
- [ ] Rollback snapshots exist for config and KV schema (S3 keys verified).
- [ ] DB migration status: none required. Confirmed by Marco.
- [ ] External partner notify list (APAC customers w/ enterprise contracts) has been emailed by CS.

Night-shift cutover watchlist (operator-facing)
- Signal codes (quick reference):
  - GREEN: metrics within baseline thresholds. Continue.
  - AMBER: transient blips; increase sampling, keep canary; open a short-lived incident channel.
  - RED: >= 0.5% user-facing errors or latency >2x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes. Pause rollout and rollback affected toggles.

- Immediate checks after each flip (template for operator)
  1) Query synthetic latency stream: compare 95th to baseline - metric key metric.latency.95p
  2) Search logs for 5xx spikes: logs.service.errors > 0.5%
  3) Token accounting: unit.cost.perk > expected change?
  4) Spot-check traces for tail-fusions in GV runtime (span name: runtime.kv.serialize)

Escalation ladder (primary -> secondary -> fallback)
- Primary on-call: Jonah Patel (call -> Slack DND override)
- Secondary SRE lead: Evelyn Park (call)
- Night liaison / exec notify: Claire Nguyen (email summary + Slack)

Immediate rollback triggers
- Any sustained 5xx increase crossing 0.5% threshold for >5m.
- Token cost explosion: >40% unexpected increase vs preflight (investigate, rollback autoscaler).
- KV cache deserialization failures observed in traces (span.error present).

Rollback quick steps (if triggered)
1) Pause routing policy toggle: revert traffic split to previous route.
2) Revert autoscaler to prior thresholds via config management (run rollback script).
3) Re-run canary at old config, validate for 30m.
4) If KV cache errors, disable KV serialization flag on affected nodes and restart pool.

Post-release validations (0-4 hours)
- 30m: sanity smoke (100 synthetic requests across tiers), compare error rates.
- 1h: user-facing metric reconciliation (billing tokens, per-route cost report).
- 2h: telemetry sampling verification (traces + logs retention checks).
- 4h: finalize roll notes and close the bridge if stable.

Draft release notes (paste-ready, trimmed)
- Title: Apr 2027 overnight cutover — autoscaler + KV cache rollout
- TL;DR: We adjusted autoscaler thresholds and rolled a KV cache serialization optimization to 50% of nodes. A routing policy update directs a portion of batch traffic to the g-quant batch path for improved throughput. No API changes; SDKs unaffected.
- What changed:
  * Autoscaler threshold increased to 60% to reduce churn during high-burst flows.
  * KV cache serialization optimization deployed to half the pool; reduces cold-start token overhead.
  * Batch routing policy toggled to prefer g-quant batch execution for eligible non-interactive requests.
- Impact: Expected lower per-token cost for batch workloads; negligible change to user latency for interactive tiers. If you see increased errors or token cost spikes, contact release-ops.
- Known issues: Intermittent deserialization warnings observed in early canary — mitigated by disabling the flag on affected nodes. If you are seeing 5xxs, please include trace id and sample request time.
- Rollback: Reverted to previous autoscaler and KV serialization state at 01:12 UTC for a small subset after an amber window; full remediation completed at 02:05 UTC.

Field notes / open questions (to follow up in retro)
- Do we need a separate APAC evening lane for future runs? Night crew needed to force a manual APAC fallback at one point.
- Autoscaler telemetry cadence was coarse; consider increasing sample rate for next release.
- Can we add a tiny alert for token-cost deltas to reduce manual looking?

Notes to self (Claire)
- Draft speak: short, factual, include timeline and who closed the loop.
- Add incident id if any post-release becomes a P1.

Attachments and quick refs
- Canary dashboard: dashboards/release/apr-2027-canary
- Cost baseline sheet: sheets/costs/apr-2027-preflight.csv
- Smoke test script: github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/blobs/smoke/sanity.sh

End of night-owl slate — leave comments inline if you were on the bridge and observed anything odd.
